compute: GPU 3, ~35 min per fold (4000 updates + 8 scorings of 400 rows + validation inference), five folds
question: Can the image-level GT HEX of the fold's thousands of training images select a better point detector (checkpoint / training length) than the fixed 1000-update recipe, without touching the 5 validation images?

design.training: identical to sg2_specialist (strong point loss, 20 train-green x 4 flips) but 4000 updates with a scoring every 500
design.score: Pearson r between log hex6_all (Voronoi of peaks >= 0.35) and log GT HEX on a fixed random subset of 400 fold-training rows (train-green and HEX = 0 rows excluded; seed 1000+fold); in-sample calibrated HEX MAPE reported alongside
design.selection: max r; only the selected checkpoint is kept; val-5 F1 is logged at every checkpoint for information only

evaluation: val-5 F1 of the selected checkpoint vs 0.666 (seed-46, 1000 updates); five-fold LOFO hex6 blend of the five selected detectors on bases A and B, alone and inside the existing 13-detector ensemble (ensemble.py)
pre_specified_decision: success (PI): ensemble hex6 blend on B <= -0.03 pp mean with HEX improving on >= 4 folds, or val-5 F1 > 0.72; secondary: whether r on fold-train rows tracks val-5 F1 across checkpoints (if it does, GT scoring is a valid model-selection signal for G1b/G1c)
falsification: if the GT score is flat or anti-correlated with val-5 F1 across checkpoints, image-level GT cannot select detectors and G1b's weak loss has no validated target.
